generatedProse.practice-connection:
Academic integrity is the ground every piece of academic work stands on. Each source you reference with purpose, each finding you weigh rather than stack, each judgement about quoting or paraphrasing, is integrity in practice. Treat what follows as being about your own essays, reports and projects, not about study in the abstract, because that is where owning it will count.

The same demand runs through professional life. Wherever your account of where ideas came from has to be trusted, integrity is the whole point, and the habit you build now is one you keep long after you graduate.
